sources.label: First-person Vodafone-to-Optus attempt blocked by identity/passport-account mismatch at online support and franchise store; exact current Flex Plus SKU and final resolution unknown
Original Optus postpaid-to-discounted yearly prepaid buyer reports manual activation friction, contradictory support and actual refund; exact Flex Plus tariff unverified

events.outcome: Legacy A$59/186-day and A$180/365-day retention economics are stale. Current official long-expiry options are A$180/186 days and A$350/365 days, while Optus states the 365-day A$350 price rises to A$395 on 2026-09-30.

events.scope: ONE Reddit OP bought discounted yearly Optus prepaid while holding EXISTING Optus postpaid number; exact current Flex Plus 365-day SKU, payment instrument and country unverified
events.outcome: The OP reports purchasing a discounted annual prepaid SIM while already on Optus postpaid; the website required manual activation to retain the number, and agents gave contradictory statements during about three hours of support. Crucial SAME-AUTHOR EDIT: the buyer refunded the entire purchase instead of completing transfer. This is actual purchase then refund with an unsuccessful SAME-OPERATOR number-migration attempt, not a proven new-number activation failure, overseas first attachment, passport check, paid-offer price, or named-app OTP. No finding that all Optus long-expiry plans are incompatible with porting.

events.scope: One Reddit original poster attempting to port an EXISTING Vodafone number to Optus with passport ID; specific prepaid/Flex Plus plan not identified; domestic support/store stage, location and nationality not verified
events.outcome: The poster says an Optus identity system associated their passport number with a different name, preventing the Vodafone-to-Optus transfer. Online support reported the same mismatch; a franchise Optus store referred them to a company-owned store. No confirmed cause, security breach, identity fraud, resolution, successful activation, actual plan SKU, overseas-new-number checkout or named-app OTP. Do not retain identity document numbers or infer every foreign passport is rejected. This is an adjacent Optus onboarding friction report, NOT a verified current Flex Plus 365-day product failure.

data.acquisitionSummary: Optus currently sells Flex Plus SIM/eSIM online. On 2026-09-29 the 365-day starter is advertised at A$199 for new services, then A$350; Optus says the A$350 price becomes A$395 from 2026-09-30.

keep.action: Current official long-expiry choices are A$180 for 186 days or A$350 for 365 days. The 365-day price is scheduled to become A$395 from 2026-09-30, so reverify before relying on a settled annual retention cost.

data.acquisitionSummary: 2026-10-12 Optus public online listing: Flex Plus 365-day starter/eSIM A$395 (350GB on activation and next two recharges, then 240GB); 186-day A$200. Prior A$199 starter promotion ended 2026-09-29 and A$350 standard 365-day rate ended 2026-09-29. This is a provider-listed price, NOT a completed checkout or a foreign-buyer eligibility test.

keep.action: Current listed Flex Plus 365-day recharge is A$395, checked 2026-10-12; the 186-day alternative lists A$200. Previous A$350/365d and A$199 new-service promotion are historical September cohorts. Existing prepaid packs purchased before the increase may retain face-value activation price and a 90-day recharge discount only if activated before 2026-12-29, per Optus restrictions. NOT a general new-buyer A$199/A$350 option.
